results.title: Group function symbols
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: The function symbols of the first-order language of groups, graded by arity, are a constant symbol for the identity (arity $0$), a symbol for inversion (arity $1$) and a symbol for multiplication (arity $2$); there are no others.

results.title: The first-order language of groups
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The first-order language of groups has the group function symbols (a constant for the identity, a unary symbol for inversion and a binary symbol for multiplication) as its function symbols and no relation symbols.

results.title: The canonical structure on a group
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a group $G$, the canonical structure on $G$ for the first-order language of groups interprets the identity constant as the identity $1$ of $G$, inversion as $x \mapsto x^{-1}$ and multiplication as $(x, y) \mapsto xy$; there are no relation symbols to interpret.

results.title: The function symbols of the language of groups
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the $n$-ary function symbols of the first-order language of groups are exactly the group function symbols of arity $n$.

results.title: The language of groups has no relation symbols
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the first-order language of groups has no $n$-ary relation symbols.

results.title: Multiplication in the canonical structure
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every group $G$ and every pair $(x_0, x_1)$ of elements of $G$, the multiplication symbol of the language of groups, interpreted in the canonical structure on $G$, sends $(x_0, x_1)$ to $x_0 x_1$.

results.title: Inversion in the canonical structure
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every group $G$ and every one-element tuple $(x_0)$ of elements of $G$, the inversion symbol of the language of groups, interpreted in the canonical structure on $G$, sends $(x_0)$ to $x_0^{-1}$.

results.title: The identity in the canonical structure
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every group $G$, the identity constant symbol of the language of groups, interpreted in the canonical structure on $G$, takes the value $1$ at the empty tuple, where $1$ is the identity of $G$.

results.title: Eigenvalues of the inverse matrix
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $M$ be a square matrix over a field $K$, with rows and columns indexed by a finite type, whose determinant is a unit of $K$ (so $M$ is invertible), and let $\mu \in K$ be nonzero. Then a vector $x$ is an eigenvector of $M$ with eigenvalue $\mu$ (that is, $x \ne 0$ and $Mx = \mu x$) if and only if $x$ is an eigenvector of $M^{-1}$ with eigenvalue $\mu^{-1}$.

results.title: Spectral theorem for normal matrices
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $M$ be a complex square matrix whose rows and columns are indexed by a finite set $n$, and write $M^*$ for its conjugate transpose. If $M$ is normal, that is, $M^* M = M M^*$, then there exist a unitary matrix $P$ indexed by $n$ (so $P^* P = P P^* = I$) and a family of complex numbers $(d_i)_{i \in n}$ such that $P^* M P$ is the diagonal matrix with diagonal entries $d_i$.

results.title: Eigenvalues under a row-sum bound
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The eigenvalues of a positive semidefinite real matrix with nonnegative entries and row sums at most `1` lie in `[0, 1]`. Nonnegativity with the row-sum bound gives the upper bound `1`, symmetry makes the eigenvalues real, and positive semidefiniteness gives the lower bound `0`; positive semidefiniteness alone gives no upper bound.

results.title: Fixed point and shifted resolvent
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let `K` be a positive semidefinite real matrix and `λ > 0`. A vector `z` satisfies the fixed-point equation `z = λ K (Y - z)` if and only if it solves the linear system `(I + λ K) z = λ K Y`, if and only if `z = (λ⁻¹ I + K)⁻¹ K Y`; and `(λ⁻¹ I + K)⁻¹ K = K (K + λ⁻¹ I)⁻¹`. results.title: Spectral radius under a row-sum bound
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A real matrix with nonnegative entries whose row sums are all at most `1` has spectral radius at most `1`. The spectral radius is that of the complexified matrix, so it bounds the modulus of every complex eigenvalue, including nonreal eigenvalues of nonsymmetric matrices. The proof bounds it by the induced `∞` operator norm, the largest absolute row sum.

results.title: Positive-definite matrices are congruent to the identity
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $P$ be a real square matrix with rows and columns indexed by a finite set, and suppose $P$ is positive definite: $P$ is symmetric and $x^{\mathsf{T}} P x > 0$ for every nonzero real vector $x$. Then there is an invertible real matrix $Q$ of the same size such that $Q^{\mathsf{T}} P Q = I$, where $I$ is the identity matrix.

results.title: Simultaneous diagonalization by congruence
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $S$ and $P$ be real square matrices with rows and columns indexed by a finite set $n$, where $S$ is symmetric and $P$ is positive definite. Then there is an invertible real matrix $C$, indexed by $n$, such that $C^{\mathsf T} S C$ is diagonal and $C^{\mathsf T} P C$ is the identity matrix.

results.title: The quotient $\mathbb{Q}_p/\mathbb{Z}_p$
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: For a prime $p$, $\mathbb{Q}_p/\mathbb{Z}_p$ is the quotient of $\mathbb{Q}_p$, viewed as a $\mathbb{Z}_p$-module, by the image of $\mathbb{Z}_p$ under the canonical inclusion $\mathbb{Z}_p \to \mathbb{Q}_p$.

results.title: Algebraic $p$-adic Pontryagin dual
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: For a prime $p$ and a $\mathbb{Z}_p$-module $A$, the algebraic $p$-adic Pontryagin dual of $A$ is the $\mathbb{Z}_p$-module $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb{Z}_p}(A, \mathbb{Q}_p/\mathbb{Z}_p)$ of all $\mathbb{Z}_p$-linear maps from $A$ to $\mathbb{Q}_p/\mathbb{Z}_p$; no topology or continuity condition is imposed.

results.title: Extensionality for the $p$-adic Pontryagin dual
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and $A$ a $\mathbb{Z}_p$-module. If two elements $\varphi, \psi$ of the algebraic $p$-adic Pontryagin dual of $A$ satisfy $\varphi(a) = \psi(a)$ for every $a \in A$, then $\varphi = \psi$.

results.title: The quotient map $\mathbb{Q}_p \to \mathbb{Q}_p/\mathbb{Z}_p$
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a prime $p$, this is the canonical projection $\mathbb{Q}_p \to \mathbb{Q}_p/\mathbb{Z}_p$, $x \mapsto x + \mathbb{Z}_p$, as a $\mathbb{Z}_p$-linear map.

results.title: The quotient map vanishes on $\mathbb{Z}_p$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a prime $p$ and every $z \in \mathbb{Z}_p$, the quotient map $\mathbb{Q}_p \to \mathbb{Q}_p/\mathbb{Z}_p$ sends the image of $z$ in $\mathbb{Q}_p$ to $0$.

results.title: The quotient map is the quotient projection
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a prime $p$ and every $x \in \mathbb{Q}_p$, the quotient map $\mathbb{Q}_p \to \mathbb{Q}_p/\mathbb{Z}_p$ sends $x$ to its class $x + \mathbb{Z}_p$ in the quotient module.

results.title: Contragredient action on the $p$-adic Pontryagin dual
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $p$ be a prime, $G$ a group and $A$ a $\mathbb{Z}_p$-module on which $G$ acts by additive maps commuting with the $\mathbb{Z}_p$-action. For $g \in G$ and $\varphi$ in the algebraic $p$-adic Pontryagin dual of $A$, $g \cdot \varphi$ is the element $a \mapsto \varphi(g^{-1} a)$ of the dual.

part.title: Straszewicz's theorem
api: Convex hull of a compact set is compact

results.title: Convex hull of a compact set is compact
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $E$ be a finite-dimensional real normed space. If $K \subseteq E$ is compact, then the convex hull of $K$ is compact.

results.title: Difference quotients
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $E$ be a real normed space and $E^*$ its continuous dual. For $h : E^* \to \mathbb{R}$ and $x, v \in E^*$, the difference quotients of $h$ at $x$ in direction $v$ form the set $\{(h(x + t v) - h(x))/t : t > 0\}$.

results.title: Directional derivative
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $E$ be a real normed space with continuous dual $E^*$. For $h : E^* \to \mathbb{R}$ and $x, v \in E^*$, the directional derivative of $h$ at $x$ in direction $v$ is the infimum of the difference quotients, $h'(x; v) = \inf_{t > 0} \frac{h(x + t v) - h(x)}{t}$, which is taken to be $0$ when these quotients are not bounded below.

results.title: Restriction of a convex function to a line
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $E$ be a real normed space with continuous dual $E^*$, and let $h : E^* \to \mathbb{R}$ be convex. For all $x, v \in E^*$, the function $s \mapsto h(x + s v)$ is convex on $\mathbb{R}$.

results.title: Difference quotients of a convex function are bounded below
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $E$ be a real normed space, $E^*$ its continuous dual, and $h : E^* \to \mathbb{R}$ a convex function. For all $x, v \in E^*$, the set of difference quotients $\{(h(x + t v) - h(x))/t : t > 0\}$ is bounded below.

results.title: Subadditivity of the directional derivative
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $E$ be a real normed space with continuous dual $E^*$, let $h : E^* \to \mathbb{R}$ be convex, and write $h'(x; v)$ for the directional derivative of $h$ at $x$ in direction $v$. For all $x, v, w \in E^*$, $h'(x; v + w) \le h'(x; v) + h'(x; w)$.

results.title: Directional derivative in direction zero
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $E$ be a real normed space with continuous dual $E^*$ and let $h : E^* \to \mathbb{R}$ be any function. For every $x \in E^*$, the directional derivative of $h$ at $x$ in direction $0$ is $0$.

results.title: Opposite directional derivatives have nonnegative sum
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $E$ be a real normed space with continuous dual $E^*$, let $h : E^* \to \mathbb{R}$ be convex, and write $h'(x; v)$ for the directional derivative of $h$ at $x$ in direction $v$. For all $x, v \in E^*$, $h'(x; v) + h'(x; -v) \ge 0$.

results.title: Support function
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a set $K$ in a real normed space $E$, the support function of $K$ sends a continuous linear functional $\ell$ on $E$ to the supremum $\sup_{x \in K} \ell(x)$ of the values of $\ell$ on $K$.

results.title: The support function of a compact set is attained
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a nonempty compact subset of a real normed space $E$, and let $h_K(l) = \sup_{x \in K} l(x)$ be its support function on the continuous dual $E^*$. For every $l \in E^*$ there is $x \in K$ with $l(x) = h_K(l)$.

results.title: The support function of a compact set is convex
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a nonempty compact subset of a real normed space $E$. Its support function $h_K(l) = \sup_{x \in K} l(x)$ is a convex function on the whole continuous dual $E^*$.

results.title: The support function of a compact set is Lipschitz
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a nonempty compact subset of a real normed space $E$, and let $h_K(l) = \sup_{x \in K} l(x)$ be its support function on the continuous dual $E^*$. There is a constant $C \ge 0$ such that $h_K(l_1) - h_K(l_2) \le C \|l_1 - l_2\|$ for all $l_1, l_2 \in E^*$, where $\|\cdot\|$ is the operator norm.

results.title: The support function of a compact set is continuous
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a nonempty compact subset of a real normed space $E$. Its support function $h_K(l) = \sup_{x \in K} l(x)$ is continuous on the continuous dual $E^*$ with the operator norm.

results.title: Gateaux points
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $E$ be a real normed space, $E^*$ its continuous dual, and $h : E^* \to \mathbb{R}$. For $x, v \in E^*$ let $h'(x; v)$ be the infimum of the difference quotients $(h(x + t v) - h(x))/t$ over $t > 0$, taken to be $0$ when they are unbounded below. A point $x \in E^*$ is a Gateaux point of $h$ when $h'(x; v) + h'(x; -v) \le 0$ for every $v \in E^*$.

results.title: Strict sublevel sets of the symmetrized directional derivative are open
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $E$ be a real normed space with continuous dual $E^*$, let $K \subseteq E$ be a nonempty compact set with support function $h_K$, and write $h_K'(x; v)$ for the directional derivative of $h_K$ at $x$ in direction $v$. For every $v \in E^*$ and every real $c$, the set of $x \in E^*$ with $h_K'(x; v) + h_K'(x; -v) < c$ is open.

results.title: Continuity of the directional derivative of a support function in the direction
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $E$ be a real normed space with continuous dual $E^*$, let $K \subseteq E$ be a nonempty compact set with support function $h_K$, and write $h_K'(x; w)$ for the directional derivative of $h_K$ at $x$ in direction $w$. For every $x \in E^*$, the map $w \mapsto h_K'(x; w)$ is continuous on $E^*$.

results.title: Lipschitz bound on directional derivatives of a support function
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $E$ be a real normed space with continuous dual $E^*$, let $K \subseteq E$ be a nonempty compact set with support function $h_K$, and write $h_K'(x; w)$ for the directional derivative of $h_K$ at $x$ in direction $w$. If $C$ is a real number with $h_K(\ell_1) - h_K(\ell_2) \le C \|\ell_1 - \ell_2\|$ for all $\ell_1, \ell_2 \in E^*$, then $h_K'(x; w) \le C \|w\|$ for all $x, w \in E^*$.

results.title: Mazur's theorem for support functions
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $E$ be a finite-dimensional real normed space with continuous dual $E^*$, let $K \subseteq E$ be a nonempty compact set with support function $h_K$, and write $h_K'(\ell; v)$ for the directional derivative of $h_K$ at $\ell$ in direction $v$. Then the Gateaux points of $h_K$, that is, the functionals $\ell \in E^*$ with $h_K'(\ell; v) + h_K'(\ell; -v) \le 0$ for every $v \in E^*$, form a dense subset of $E^*$.

results.title: A maximizer bounds the directional derivative of the support function from below
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a nonempty compact subset of a real normed space $E$, let $h_K(l) = \sup_{y \in K} l(y)$ be its support function on the continuous dual $E^*$, and write $h_K'(u; v)$ for the directional derivative of $h_K$ at $u$ in direction $v$. If $u \in E^*$ and $z \in K$ satisfy $u(z) = h_K(u)$, then $v(z) \le h_K'(u; v)$ for every $v \in E^*$.

results.title: Maximizers at a Gateaux point of the support function are unique
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a nonempty compact subset of a real normed space $E$, and let $h_K(l) = \sup_{y \in K} l(y)$ be its support function on the continuous dual $E^*$. If $l \in E^*$ is a Gateaux point of $h_K$ and $z_1, z_2 \in K$ satisfy $l(z_1) = h_K(l)$ and $l(z_2) = h_K(l)$, then $z_1 = z_2$.

results.title: A unique maximizer of a linear functional is an exposed point
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a nonempty compact set in a real normed space $E$, let $\ell$ be a continuous linear functional on $E$, and let $h_K$ be the support function of $K$. If $z \in K$ satisfies $\ell(z) = h_K(\ell)$ and every $y \in K$ with $\ell(y) = h_K(\ell)$ equals $z$, then $z$ is an exposed point of $K$.

results.title: Straszewicz's theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $E$ be a finite-dimensional real normed space and let $A \subseteq E$ be a compact convex set. Then every extreme point of $A$ lies in the closure of the set of exposed points of $A$.

results.summary: For real numbers $a$ and $b$, let $A = (0, 0)$, $B = (a, 0)$ and $C = (0, b)$. The lune on the horizontal leg is the set of points $x = (x_1, x_2)$ of the closed disk with diameter $AB$ satisfying $a x_2 \le 0$ that do not lie in the half-disk on the hypotenuse, the set of points of the closed disk with diameter $BC$ satisfying $b x_1 + a x_2 \le ab$. For $a, b > 0$ this is the set of points of the closed lower…

results.title: Hippocrates lune on the vertical leg
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For real numbers $a$ and $b$, the vertical lune is the set of points $(x, y) \in \mathbb{R}^2$ with $x^2 + (y - b/2)^2 \le b^2/4$ and $bx \le 0$ that do not satisfy both $(x - a/2)^2 + (y - b/2)^2 \le (a^2 + b^2)/4$ and $bx + ay \le ab$.

results.title: Right triangle with legs on the axes
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For real numbers $a$ and $b$, the right triangle $T(a, b)$ is the convex hull in the plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ of the three points $(0, 0)$, $(a, 0)$ and $(0, b)$.

results.title: Hippocrates' theorem on lunes
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $a, b > 0$ and consider the right triangle with vertices $A = (0, 0)$, $B = (a, 0)$ and $C = (0, b)$. The Lebesgue measure of the lune on the horizontal leg plus the Lebesgue measure of the lune on the vertical leg equals the Lebesgue measure of the triangle, that is, of the convex hull of $A$, $B$ and $C$.

results.title: Normalized expectation value of an observable
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The normalized real expectation is Mathlib's canonical Rayleigh quotient. For a nonzero state and self-adjoint observable it is the physical expectation. At zero this total definition is zero; zero is not a physical state.

results.title: Normalized expectation on a unit vector
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: On a unit vector, normalized expectation equals the original quadratic mean.

results.title: Centered state vector of an observable
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The centered vector subtracts the normalized real expectation times the state. Its squared norm divided by the squared state norm is `variance`.

results.title: Normalized variance of an observable
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Normalized variance is the centered squared norm divided by the squared state norm. For a nonzero state and self-adjoint observable it is the physical variance. The totalized value at zero is zero. Off the unit sphere this corrects the raw quadratic quantities; agreement with the original formulas is asserted only for unit states.

results.title: Normalized variance on the unit sphere
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: On the unit sphere, normalized variance is the centered squared norm.

results.title: Normalized variance is invariant under nonzero scaling
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Nonzero scalar multiplication does not change normalized variance.

results.title: Expectation inner product of a self-adjoint operator
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a self-adjoint operator, the expectation inner product is the normalized mean multiplied by the squared state norm. The norm factor is required off the unit sphere.

results.title: Flipped expectation inner product of a self-adjoint operator
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The flipped expectation has the same necessary squared-state-norm factor.

results.title: Inner product of two centered vectors
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The inner product of two centered vectors, for self-adjoint operators at a unit vector: the uncentered inner product minus the product of the mean values.

results.title: Commutator expectation as the skew part of the centered inner product
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The commutator expectation is the skew part of the inner product of the centered vectors.

results.title: Commutator expectation of self-adjoint operators is purely imaginary
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The commutator expectation of two self-adjoint operators is purely imaginary: its real part vanishes.

results.title: Squared norm of the commutator expectation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The squared norm of the commutator expectation is four times the squared imaginary part of the centered inner product.

results.title: Norm of the commutator expectation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The commutator expectation has norm twice the absolute imaginary part of the centered inner product.

results.title: Robertson–Schrödinger uncertainty principle
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The Robertson–Schrödinger uncertainty principle: the product of the variances is at least the squared covariance plus a quarter of the squared norm of the commutator expectation.

results.title: Robertson's uncertainty principle
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The product of the variances is at least a quarter of the squared norm of the commutator expectation.

results.title: Commutator of commuting operators vanishes
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The commutator of commuting operators vanishes.

results.title: Variance as second moment minus squared mean
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The variance is the second moment minus the squared mean.

results.title: Wandering subspace of an isometry
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The wandering subspace of an isometry `V`: the orthogonal complement of its range. Vectors here are orthogonal to every vector in the range of `V`.

results.title: Powers of an isometry preserve inner products
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Pulling inner products back along powers of an isometry.

results.title: Positive powers of an isometry land in its range
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A positive power of an isometry lands in the range of the isometry.

results.title: Orthogonality of pushed-forward wandering vectors
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A wandering vector, pushed forward `k` times, is orthogonal to any vector pushed forward strictly more times.

results.title: Orthogonality of pushed-forward wandering vectors, symmetric form
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The symmetric form of `inner_pow_wandering`.

results.title: Wandering subspace and range are complementary
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The ambient space splits as the wandering subspace plus the range.

results.title: One-step Wold splitting into wandering vector plus range
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: One step of the Wold decomposition: every vector splits as a wandering vector plus a vector in the range.

results.title: Finite Wold decomposition
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Finite Wold decomposition: every vector is a finite sum of pushed-forward wandering vectors plus a remainder in the range of `V ^ n`. The wandering coefficients vanish at and beyond `n`.

results.title: Pythagorean identity for the Wold decomposition
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Pythagoras for a Wold decomposition: the squared norm of a vector is the sum of the squared norms of its wandering coefficients plus the squared norm of the remainder.

results.title: Uniqueness of the finite Wold decomposition
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Uniqueness of the Wold decomposition at level `n`: the remainder and the finite wandering sum are uniquely determined.

results.title: Residual subspace of an isometry
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The residual subspace of an isometry: vectors in the range of every power of `V`.

results.title: An isometry maps its residual subspace into itself
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The isometry maps its residual subspace into itself.

results.title: Residual subspace is orthogonal to the wandering part
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The residual subspace is orthogonal to every pushed-forward wandering vector: the wandering part and the residual part of Wold's decomposition are orthogonal.

results.title: Isometry restricted to the residual subspace is bijective
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The restriction of an isometry to its residual subspace is bijective.

results.title: Isometry restricted to the residual subspace preserves inner products
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The restriction of an isometry to its residual subspace preserves inner products.

results.title: Unitary part of an isometry on its residual subspace
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The isometry restricts to a unitary operator (a linear isometric equivalence) on its residual subspace.

results.title: Action of the residual unitary of an isometry
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Applying the residual unitary is the same as applying `V` and viewing the result in the ambient space.

results.title: Kadec–Klee property, all-functionals form
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $E$ be a uniformly convex real normed space, let $(u_n)$ be a sequence in $E$ and let $x \in E$. If $f(u_n) \to f(x)$ for every continuous linear functional $f \colon E \to \mathbb{R}$ and $\|u_n\| \to \|x\|$, then $u_n \to x$ in norm.

results.title: Kadec–Klee property, weak-topology form
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $E$ be a uniformly convex real normed space, let $(u_n)$ be a sequence in $E$ and let $x \in E$. If $u_n \to x$ in the weak topology of $E$ (the topology induced by the continuous linear functionals $E \to \mathbb{R}$) and $\|u_n\| \to \|x\|$, then $u_n \to x$ in norm.

results.title: Kadec–Klee iff, all-functionals form
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $E$ be a uniformly convex real normed space, let $(u_n)$ be a sequence in $E$ and let $x \in E$. Then $u_n \to x$ in norm if and only if $f(u_n) \to f(x)$ for every continuous linear functional $f \colon E \to \mathbb{R}$ and $\|u_n\| \to \|x\|$.

results.title: Kadec–Klee iff, weak-topology form
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $E$ be a uniformly convex real normed space, let $(u_n)$ be a sequence in $E$ and let $x \in E$. Then $u_n \to x$ in norm if and only if $u_n \to x$ in the weak topology of $E$ (the topology induced by the continuous linear functionals $E \to \mathbb{R}$) and $\|u_n\| \to \|x\|$.

results.title: Every algebra of sets is a semiring of sets
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If $\mathcal{A}$ is an algebra of sets on $\alpha$, then $\mathcal{A}$ is a semiring of sets: $\emptyset \in \mathcal{A}$, $s \cap t \in \mathcal{A}$ for all $s, t \in \mathcal{A}$, and for all $s, t \in \mathcal{A}$ the difference $s \setminus t$ is the union of finitely many pairwise disjoint members of $\mathcal{A}$.

results.title: Tao's small-doubling question (AIM Problem 3.5)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The proposition that small doubling forces small tripling uniformly in all groups: there is a function $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ such that for every group $G$, every finite nonempty subset $A \subseteq G$ and every real number $K$, if $|A \cdot A| \le K |A|$ then $|A \cdot A \cdot A| \le f(K) |A|$. Here $A \cdot A = \{ab : a, b \in A\}$ and $A \cdot A \cdot A = \{abc : a, b, c \in A\}$.

results.title: Small doubling does not imply small tripling
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There is no function $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ such that for every group $G$, every finite nonempty subset $A \subseteq G$ and every real number $K$ with $|A \cdot A| \le K |A|$ one has $|A \cdot A \cdot A| \le f(K) |A|$. Here $A \cdot A = \{ab : a, b \in A\}$ and $A \cdot A \cdot A = \{abc : a, b, c \in A\}$.

results.title: Sum-free set
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $G$ be a set with an addition. A subset $S \subseteq G$ is sum-free if $x + y \notin S$ for all $x, y \in S$, where $x = y$ is allowed; that is, $S$ contains no Schur triple $x + y = z$ with $x, y, z \in S$.

results.title: Distinct sum-free sets
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $G$ be a set with an addition. A subset $S \subseteq G$ is distinct sum-free if there are no pairwise distinct $x, y, z \in S$ with $x + y = z$, that is, if $S$ contains no distinct Schur triple.

results.title: Sum-free sets are distinct sum-free
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every set $G$ with an addition, every sum-free subset of $G$ is distinct sum-free.

results.title: The empty set is sum-free
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every set $G$ with an addition, the empty subset of $G$ is sum-free.

results.title: Size of a largest sum-free subset
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $G$ be a set with an addition and $S \subseteq G$. Write $\mu(S)$ for the supremum in $\mathbb{N}$ of the sizes of the finite sum-free subsets of $S$ (sets $T$ with $x + y \notin T$ for all $x, y \in T$), taken to be $0$ if these sizes are unbounded. For finite $S$ this is the largest size of a sum-free subset of $S$, and $\mu(G)$ is the value for $S = G$.

results.title: Trivial bound on sum-free subsets
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a set with an addition. For every finite subset $S \subseteq G$, the largest size of a sum-free subset of $S$ is at most $|S|$.

results.title: Number of maximal sum-free sets
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a set $G$ with an addition, $f_{\max}(G)$ is the number of maximal sum-free subsets of $G$, that is, of sets $S \subseteq G$ with $x + y \notin S$ for all $x, y \in S$ (including $x = y$) that are not properly contained in another such set; it is $0$ if there are infinitely many.

results.title: Number of maximal distinct sum-free sets
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $G$ be a set with an addition. The number $f^*_{\max}(G)$ is the number of subsets of $G$ that are maximal, with respect to inclusion, among the distinct sum-free subsets of $G$, and it is $0$ if there are infinitely many such subsets. Here $S \subseteq G$ is distinct sum-free if $x + y \notin S$ for all $x, y \in S$ such that $x$, $y$ and $x + y$ are pairwise distinct.

results.title: Number of distinct Schur triples
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a subset $F$ of a set $G$ with an addition, this is the number of ordered pairs $(x, y)$ with $x, y \in F$ such that $x$, $y$ and $x + y$ are pairwise distinct and $x + y \in F$, that is, the number of ordered distinct Schur triples $(x, y, x + y)$ in $F$. If there are infinitely many such pairs, the value is $0$ by convention.

results.title: Groups of type I(p)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $G$ be a finite set and $p$ a natural number. $G$ is of type $\mathrm{I}(p)$ if $p$ is the smallest prime with $p \equiv 2 \pmod 3$ dividing $|G|$: that is, $p$ is prime, $p \equiv 2 \pmod 3$, $p$ divides $|G|$, and $p \le q$ for every prime $q$ with $q \equiv 2 \pmod 3$ that divides $|G|$.

results.title: Characterization of type I(p)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a finite set and $p$ a natural number. Then $G$ is of type $\mathrm{I}(p)$ if and only if $p$ is prime, $p \equiv 2 \pmod 3$, $p$ divides $|G|$, and $p \le q$ for every prime $q$ with $q \equiv 2 \pmod 3$ that divides $|G|$.

results.title: Number of maximal independent sets
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a graph $\Gamma$, $\mathrm{mis}(\Gamma)$ is the number of maximal independent sets of $\Gamma$, that is, of sets of pairwise non-adjacent vertices that are not properly contained in another such set; it is $0$ if there are infinitely many.

results.title: Loops of the distinct link graph
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $G$ be a set with an addition and $S \subseteq G$. An element $x \in G$ carries a loop in the distinct link graph of $S$ if there are distinct $s, s' \in S$, both different from $x$, with $s + s' = x$, $x + s = s'$ or $x + s' = s$. In an abelian group this says exactly that $\{x, s, s'\}$ is a distinct Schur triple for some distinct $s, s' \in S$.

results.title: Independent sets of the distinct link graph
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $G$ be a set with an addition and let $S, B, I \subseteq G$. The set $I$ is an independent set of the distinct link graph $L^*_S[B]$ (the graph on vertex set $B$ given by the edges and loops of the distinct link graph of $S$) if $I \subseteq B$, no element of $I$ carries a loop, and no two elements of $I$ are adjacent.

results.title: The empty set is independent in the distinct link graph
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every set $G$ with an addition and all $S, B \subseteq G$, the empty set is an independent set of the distinct link graph $L^*_S[B]$.

results.title: Counting subgroups by order and by index
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: In a finite abelian group $G$, for every natural number $k$ the number of subgroups of order $k$ equals the number of subgroups of index $k$.

results.title: Characteristic function of a set of naturals
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The characteristic function of a set $p$ of natural numbers is the partial function $\mathbb{N} \rightharpoonup \mathbb{N}$ that is defined at every $n$, with value $1$ if $n \in p$ and value $0$ otherwise.

results.title: A set is decidable iff its characteristic function is partial recursive
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A set $p$ of natural numbers is decidable (computable as a predicate) if and only if its characteristic function is partial recursive.

results.title: Decidability transfers down Turing reducibility
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ and $q$ be sets of natural numbers such that the characteristic function of $p$ is Turing reducible to the characteristic function of $q$. If $q$ is decidable, then $p$ is decidable.

results.title: Halting set
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Fix the standard bijective numbering $n \mapsto c_n$ of the codes of partial recursive functions $\mathbb{N} \rightharpoonup \mathbb{N}$. The halting set is the set of natural numbers $n$ such that the partial recursive function with code $c_n$ is defined at $0$.

results.title: The halting set is not Turing reducible to a decidable set
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every decidable set $q$ of natural numbers, the characteristic function of the halting set is not Turing reducible to the characteristic function of $q$.

results.title: Many-one reducibility implies Turing reducibility
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If $p$ and $q$ are sets of natural numbers and $p$ is many-one reducible to $q$, that is, there is a computable $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ with $n \in p \iff f(n) \in q$ for all $n$, then the characteristic function of $p$ is Turing reducible to the characteristic function of $q$.

results.title: Every set is Turing equivalent to its complement
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every set $p$ of natural numbers, the characteristic function of the complement $\mathbb{N} \setminus p$ and the characteristic function of $p$ are Turing equivalent: each is Turing reducible to the other.

results.title: The complement of the halting set is not many-one reducible to it
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There is no computable function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ such that, for every $n$, $n$ is outside the halting set if and only if $f(n)$ is in the halting set.
